_comment: CRuby -> mruby API map for convert_mrbgem.rb. kind: call (rename; inject mrb as first arg when inject_mrb), macro (rename or identity, no mrb), expr (identifier replaced by an expression), type (identifier replaced), special (handled by converter code), refuse (no equivalent; marker left in output). needs_mrb marks identifiers that require an mrb_state in scope. Any CRuby-looking identifier missing from this file is refused by the converter.

rb_const_get_at.reason: no exact mruby equivalent: mrb_const_get also searches the superclass chain, rb_const_get_at looks only in the receiver

rb_ensure.reason: no direct mruby equivalent (ensure callback not in the supported subset)

rb_rescue.reason: no direct mruby equivalent (rescue callback not in the supported subset)

rb_rescue2.reason: no direct mruby equivalent (rescue callback not in the supported subset)

Check_Type.reason: type-check macro not in the supported subset

rb_check_type.reason: type-check function not in the supported subset

rb_gc_register_address.reason: address form (VALUE *): mruby has no address root. mrb_gc_register roots a value, so a later store through the address would not be rooted; the rooting must be designed by hand

rb_gc_register_mark_object.caveat: mrb_gc_register keeps the value in mruby's root table (src/gc.c:564) for the life of the state; CRuby never unregisters it either. Immediate values need no root and are ignored by mrb_gc_register

rb_gc_mark.reason: no mark callback in mruby: mrb_data_type has only dfree and ivars (include/mruby/data.h), so a mark function would never be called and rb_gc_mark has no place to run

rb_gc_mark_movable.reason: no mark callback in mruby: mrb_data_type has only dfree and ivars (include/mruby/data.h), so a mark function would never be called and rb_gc_mark has no place to run (movable marking has no mruby form either)

rb_gc_enable.reason: no mruby enable function: gc.disabled is a VM flag (include/mruby/gc.h), and CRuby's return value (the previous state) would have to be emulated

rb_gc_disable.reason: no mruby disable function: gc.disabled is a VM flag (include/mruby/gc.h), and CRuby's return value (the previous state) would have to be emulated

StringValuePtr.caveat: argument must already be a String: no implicit to_str conversion

StringValueCStr.caveat: argument must already be a String: no to_str conversion and no NUL-byte check

NUM2ULONG.caveat: signed conversion: unsigned range is not checked

rb_str_new_frozen.caveat: returns a copy; the copy is not frozen

rb_thread_call_without_gvl.caveat: modelled on mruby-uv: func runs on the libuv thread pool and the caller runs the loop until it finishes; ubf is ignored (no interrupt)

rb_ext_ractor_safe.reason: ractor declaration; mruby has no ractors, so the declaration has no effect

rb_intern_const.caveat: argument must be a string literal (mrb_intern_lit is a macro over mrb_intern_static); a char pointer does not compile

rb_hash_aset.caveat: mruby returns void; the CRuby return value (the stored value) is not available

rb_ary_push.caveat: mruby returns void; the CRuby return value (the array) is not available

RARRAY_AREF.caveat: CRuby reads the element pointer without a bounds check; mruby returns nil out of range and accepts negative offsets

rb_utf8_str_new.caveat: mruby strings carry no encoding: the bytes are copied unchanged and UTF-8 is not recorded

rb_obj_class.caveat: returns struct RClass *, not mrb_value: wrap with mrb_obj_value() where a VALUE is needed

rb_respond_to.caveat: returns mrb_bool (0 or 1), where CRuby returns int

rb_ivar_set.caveat: mruby returns void; the CRuby return value (the value) is not available

INT2FIX.caveat: no range check: the mruby fixnum range depends on the value boxing

LONG2FIX.caveat: no range check: the mruby fixnum range depends on the value boxing

FIX2INT.caveat: no check that the value is a fixnum; the result is mrb_int, not int

FIX2LONG.caveat: no check that the value is a fixnum; the result is mrb_int

rb_type.caveat: returns enum mrb_vtype: compare only with MRB_TT_* values. nil and false both report MRB_TT_FALSE (mruby/boxing_nan.h), so T_NIL and T_FALSE are not mapped

Qundef.caveat: mrb_value is a struct: test with mrb_undef_p(), not with ==

T_DATA.caveat: CRuby T_DATA also covers TypedData; MRB_TT_CDATA is the nearest mruby C-data type, so check each use

rb_global_variable.reason: address form (VALUE *), as rb_gc_register_address: no mruby equivalent (mrb_gc_register roots a value, not a variable)

rb_str_cat.caveat: the length is not checked for sign: a negative length becomes a large size_t

rb_str_buf_new.caveat: capa is a size hint only: the new string is empty, as in CRuby

rb_utf8_str_new_cstr.caveat: mruby strings carry no encoding: the bytes are copied unchanged and UTF-8 is not recorded

rb_str_freeze.caveat: mrb_obj_freeze freezes any object; CRuby's rb_str_freeze takes a String

rb_str_append.caveat: no encoding compatibility check (mruby has no encodings); CRuby raises Encoding::CompatibilityError for incompatible encodings

RHASH_SIZE.caveat: returns mrb_int (signed), where CRuby returns size_t

NUM2DBL.caveat: needs float support (not MRB_NO_FLOAT); nil and non-numeric values raise TypeError as in CRuby, with mruby's message

rb_num2dbl.caveat: needs float support (not MRB_NO_FLOAT); nil and non-numeric values raise TypeError as in CRuby, with mruby's message

ULONG2NUM.caveat: no range check: an unsigned value above the mrb_int maximum wraps negative

ULL2NUM.caveat: no range check: an unsigned value above the mrb_int maximum wraps negative

NUM2LL.caveat: mrb_int may be narrower than long long: values outside its range are not preserved

rb_id2name.caveat: the pointer is into mruby's symbol table: valid until the state is closed

rb_id2str.caveat: mruby does not promise a frozen result, as CRuby's rb_id2str does

rb_to_id.caveat: accepts only Symbol and String: CRuby also converts other objects with to_str

rb_block_given_p.caveat: returns mrb_bool (0 or 1), where CRuby returns int

rb_const_defined.caveat: a module receiver does not fall back to Object, as in rb_const_get; returns mrb_bool

rb_const_defined_at.caveat: returns mrb_bool, where CRuby returns int

RB_LIKELY.caveat: the branch-prediction hint is dropped; !!(x) has the same 0 or 1 value as the GCC definition of RB_LIKELY

RB_UNLIKELY.caveat: the branch-prediction hint is dropped; !!(x) has the same 0 or 1 value as the GCC definition of RB_UNLIKELY

rb_class2name.caveat: CRuby first skips singleton and include classes (rb_class_real); mrb_class_name does not. An anonymous class gets a new name string, and the pointer into it can dangle after the next GC (a named class keeps its path string alive)

rb_undef_method.caveat: the first argument is a struct RClass *, not a VALUE; a class variable there is passed unwrapped (special_arg_positions_class_only)

SYM2ID.caveat: no check that the value is a Symbol; the result is mrb_sym (the mapped type of ID), not an unsigned long

T_FALSE.caveat: mruby's nil also has type MRB_TT_FALSE (mrb_nil_p tells them apart by value), so this matches nil, which CRuby reports as T_NIL; RB_TYPE_P(x, T_FALSE) stays refused for this reason

RUBY_T_FIXNUM.caveat: mruby has no bignum, so MRB_TT_INTEGER matches every Integer, including values CRuby reports as T_BIGNUM; RB_TYPE_P(x, T_FIXNUM) stays refused for this reason

T_FIXNUM.caveat: mruby has no bignum, so MRB_TT_INTEGER matches every Integer, including values CRuby reports as T_BIGNUM; RB_TYPE_P(x, T_FIXNUM) stays refused for this reason

rb_eIndexError.caveat: struct RClass *, as E_ARGUMENT_ERROR: a VALUE use needs mrb_obj_value(); in rb_raise it is the class argument

rb_eRangeError.caveat: struct RClass *, as E_ARGUMENT_ERROR: a VALUE use needs mrb_obj_value(); in rb_raise it is the class argument

rb_warn.caveat: prints on every call; CRuby's rb_warn is silent when $VERBOSE is nil. Output is 'warning: ' and the message on stderr, with no file or line; PRIsVALUE is not supported

rb_sys_fail.caveat: raises SystemCallError (with the errno) only when mruby-errno defines it; otherwise RuntimeError with the message, which mruby does not allow to be NULL

rb_obj_classname.caveat: an anonymous class gets a new name string, and the pointer into it can dangle after the next GC (a named class keeps its path string alive), as for rb_class2name

rb_sym2id.caveat: no check that the value is a Symbol; the result is mrb_sym (the mapped type of ID), not an unsigned long

rb_warning.caveat: prints on every call: CRuby's rb_warning prints only in verbose mode ($VERBOSE true), and rb_warn always prints. Output is 'warning: ' and the message on stderr, with no file or line; PRIsVALUE is not supported

rb_gc_location.caveat: identity: mruby's collector never moves objects (no relocation API in include/ or src/gc.c), so the location is the value itself; the argument stays in parentheses
